question: Why cannot the great lord be confined to a single limited form?
premises: If confined to one form, he would lose great-lordship and consciousness.
Limited luminosity is the mark of the inert, like a pot.
inference: The great lord cannot be limited, because limitation belongs to inert things.
plain_english: He would abandon his great-lordship and his nature as consciousness, like a pot and other inert things; for limited luminosity is indeed the mark of the inert.
